blind_target.authors: Seidel E-M, Habel U, Finkelmeyer A, Schneider F, Gur RC, Derntl B.
blind_target.title: Implicit and explicit behavioral tendencies in male and female depression.
blind_target.evidence_quote: Although we do not have previous genetic research to base our hypotheses on, based on clinical experiences, information processing theories in depression and the research by Seidel and colleagues [ 42 ], we expected avoidance of negative (sad, angry) facial expressions in remitted depressed S/L g -carriers who have experienced childhood trauma, as this represents the most vulnerable subgroup.
blind_target.outcome_quote: In line with Seidel and colleagues [ 42 ], we expected automatic avoidance of angry faces as well. We did not find this, however.
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: The specific re-tested Seidel finding is automatic avoidance of angry faces, explicitly not found. New sad-face/genetic interaction results are not a successful replication of Seidel’s angry-face effect.

luna_triage.reason: The introduction identifies Seidel et al.’s specific result—automatic avoidance in response to angry faces—and the discussion explicitly says the present study expected that same result but did not find it. This is a direct empirical retest despite the paper’s conceptual focus on genetic and trauma associations. The shipped Vrijsen et al. (2014) paper is distinct from Seidel et al. (2010).
luna_triage.omission_quote: In line with Seidel and colleagues [ 42 ], we expected automatic avoidance of angry faces as well. We did not find this, however.
luna_triage.identity_quote: Seidel and colleagues [ 42 ], for example, found that depressed patients showed automatic avoidance in response to angry faces.

quality_gate: Luna is triage only. Independently establish actual empirical retesting and absence under ALL shipped identities/alternate reports. Read prior objections. No paper outcome is being requested.
